note.backdrop: Wednesday ended almost where Tuesday did, after a hard morning. The Nasdaq 100 fund closed -0.65% after being -4.38% at 11:02 a.m. ET; the S&P 500 fund closed -0.29% and the Dow fund +0.31% (StockTitan). After the close the funds edged up: S&P 500 fund +0.5%, Nasdaq 100 fund +0.4%, small caps +0.5%, futures +0.4% (k). Oil +2.8%, gold +1.8% and bitcoin +2.0% since the close, each inside its usual day (d:oil, d:gold, d:bitcoin). Of 2,453 stocks one is outside its 9-in-10 range and seven outside their 2-in-3 range: a thin evening before Thanksgiving, in which one piece of news moved two stocks and several others moved on a single trade. US markets are closed on Thursday and close at 1 p.m. ET on Friday.

read.says: Nov 25 close: QQQ -0.65% (after -4.38% at 11:02 a.m. ET), SPY -0.29%, DIA +0.31%; Nvidia -3.91% to $149.30, about 40% of Monday's +31.48% given back; Micron -4.53%; AMD -1.75%, 4.3% below Friday's close; Anthropic closed at $82.79, under its $83.00 IPO price; CNBC reported S&P Global Ratings put Nvidia's credit rating on watch for a possible cut, citing how the company is managed and governed; Dell closed +0.60%; Deere closed +4.44% after forecasting fiscal 2027 net income of $4.50 to $5.25 billion against $4.860 billion this year; Pharming -23.98% after pausing production of RUCONEST; at 7:59 p.m. ET SPY +0.52% and QQQ +0.42% from the close; US markets closed Thursday, Friday closes at 1 p.m. ET; tariff comments due Jan 5, 2027.

Vertex: the FDA told it on Nov 24 that it extends the target date for its decision on povetacicept in IgA nephropathy by up to three months, from Nov 30, 2026 to no later than Feb 28, 2027; the agency asked for information late in the review and classed Vertex's reply as a major amendment; Vertex says it is confident in the data.

Vertex fell after hours on the FDA's delay; Vera Therapeutics, whose TRUTAKNA won accelerated approval in July 2026 for the same kidney disease, rose more than 17% after hours as head-to-head competition is put off.

Sep 9, 2026: people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg that Kinetik was in the early stages of exploring alternatives and preparing a possible sale process that could begin within weeks; no final decision; in February the Financial Times reported an approach from Western Midstream that produced no deal.

themes.beneath: In money the two moves are far apart. 7.3% of Vertex's $144.0 bn is about $10.5 bn; 16.7% of Vera's $2.1 bn is about $0.35 bn (n:VRTX, n:VERA). Three months of delay alone is small against $10.5 bn. My inference: the price holds some chance that this review does not end in approval, and gives back a run into the date: Vertex rose 4.8% against the market on Tuesday and touched its 52-week high on Wednesday (h:VRTX, s1). Vertex's release says the FDA generally takes this step when new information could settle open questions inside the same review; that is the company's reading. Vera is fragile in another way: its cash and equivalents cover about half a quarter of its losses, investments not counted, and before this jump the mosaic put a sale of new shares in the next 20 sessions at 6.7% against 0.9% for the usual stock, with a registration on file (n:VERA, z:VERA). That chance is tested as a chance (P1a PASS), not as a direction (P1b FAIL).
themes.cause: Vertex said at 4:02 p.m. ET that the FDA told it on Nov 24 it needs up to three more months to decide on povetacicept for IgA nephropathy: the target date moves from Nov 30, 2026 to no later than Feb 28, 2027, after a late request for information whose answer the agency classed as a major amendment (the Vertex release; s3). Vertex -7.3% after the close and Vera Therapeutics +16.7% (s2).
themes.mechanism: Vera's TRUTAKNA won accelerated approval in July 2026 for the same disease (s2): each month Vertex's drug is not on the market is a month Vera sells without it, and Vertex loses the launch expected this year. Both moves are the stocks' own: the market carried +0.1% of Vertex's and +0.5% of Vera's (x:VRTX, x:VERA), and neither one's partners moved (c1).
themes.name: A kidney-drug decision is put back three months
themes.watch: Friday's half session: whether the two moves hold on regular-session volume. A decision can come any day up to Feb 28, 2027. A sale of new shares by Vera.

themes.beneath: Of Monday's jump on the chief executive's return, Nvidia has given back about 40% ($149.30 against $165.05 on Monday and $125.53 on Friday), Micron about 94%, and AMD all of it: it closed 4.3% below Friday (StockTitan). Anthropic closed at $82.79, under its $83.00 offering price (StockTitan). Two sessions after the relief the question is no longer who runs Nvidia but what AI spending is worth: a ratings agency now names governance as a credit risk, and the memory-cost squeeze that Ambarella named on Tuesday is still there (Ambarella closed -19.77%, StockTitan). Reported: the closes and the rating watch. My inference: a rebound of one to two percent after the close is small against the two-day fall and says little.

After the close they rose a little with the funds: Nvidia +1.3%, Micron +2.3%, Lam Research +2.2%, AMD +1.9% as the check read them (k).
